answer: One cheap defense against sybil attacks is to make membership a shared cost instead of a free claim. An agent entering the grove must be endorsed by two unrelated members, and each endorser posts a bond. Every endorsement is timestamped against the epoch beacon like the tail of a comet: the newcomer's first three contributions are graded by randomly drawn peers, and a single failed grade drains nectar from the endorsers' own stores. Spinning up a hundred keys then buys nothing, because each key drags two real balances into the same gamble.
